messages:
Marta: heads-up — customer reported a sharp spike in 429s this morning while ingesting very large contexts (~60k tokens). They saw it mostly during bursts when concurrency hit ~8. Happens across multiple regions but primarily us-west1. They say their app retries immediately which amplifies the spike. example request-id: req_0a12b3c4. Posted at 09:32 UTC :wave:

Sam: thanks Marta — can you paste a minimal repro / sample curl and the X-Request-ID values when they saw 429s? also include whether they used streaming or non-streaming. quick ask to the customer: can you try with concurrency=2 and see if errors persist? :thinking:

Marta: customer sent this curl earlier (redacted keys):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rwft-xlarge-v2","input":"<~60k tokens...>","max_tokens":1024}'
```
They said `stream=false`, and their client creates 8 concurrent inflight requests. sample response header when they got a 429: `X-RateLimit-Limit: 1500`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-Request-ID: req_0a12b3c4`. Body was generic 429 with `retry_after` sometimes present, sometimes not.

Priya: pinging SRE — from the headers it looks like they exhausted a rolling TPM bucket. with ~60k tokens per request the token accounting burns fast and RPM/TPM limits become the dominant throttle even if per-request concurrency limit isn't hit. also long contexts increase server-side processing time which can cause queueing and spike perceived concurrency. can you grab the ingress logs for that request-id and time window? :eyes:

eng-bot: new logs pulled for req_0a12b3c4 (window 09:25-09:40 UTC) — attached snippet below.
```
[09:31:12] req_0a12b3c4 START model=rwft-xlarge-v2 tokens_in=59820 tokens_out=1024 concurrency_slot=7
[09:31:34] req_0a12b3c4 QUEUED queue_ms=1540 reason="burst_control"
[09:31:58] req_0a12b3c4 THROTTLED code=429 quota_type="model_tpm" limit=1500 window_s=60 remaining=0
[09:31:59] req_0a12b3c4 END status=429
```

Jorge: that log is pretty clear — this is model-level TPM exhaustion. two notes: (1) long contexts count toward TPM the same as any other tokens, so a single 60k-token request is extremely expensive; (2) burst control queueing will try to smooth traffic, but once the rolling token window is exhausted you get 429s.

Jorge: short-term playbook for support to propose to the customer:
- reduce concurrency to 2-4 while they batch/process huge contexts
- add exponential backoff on 429s (jittered) so retries don't instantly re-exhaust the TPM bucket
- if possible, split 60k contexts into multiple requests with prefix KV cache or condense the prompt (trimming system messages, compressing embeddings)
- consider streaming if they only need the tail output (reduces time-in-service and queueing)

Sam: passing suggested repro steps to the customer now. also asked them to run a short test: 1) single request with 60k context 2) two concurrent 60k requests 3) eight concurrent 8k-sliced requests to compare token burn / 429 behavior. will share results. :thumbsup:

Marta: update from customer — they ran the 8k-sliced test and the 429s disappeared. they also reduced concurrency to 3 and added 200-600ms jittered backoff; errors have fallen to near zero. they want to understand whether we have documented per-model TPM/RPM and concurrency caps.

Priya: follow-ups we should do internally:
- confirm and publish model-specific TPM/RPM recommendations in support docs (call out long-context accounting)
- add clearer 429 payloads for quota_type (e.g., `{"error":{"type":"quota_exceeded","quota_type":"model_tpm","retry_after":45}}`) so clients can react programmatically
- instrument Console with token-consumption heatmaps per-route so customers can see TPM burn in real time

Jorge: agreed. engineering will also add a small runtime improvement: explicit queue logs will include `quota_type` and `remaining` in the body for easier triage. opened ENG-3472 to track. ETA for rollout to staging: 2w.

Sam: noted. closing loop with customer; they asked if Dedicated reservations avoid this — answer: dedicated capacity can give more predictable throughput and higher limits depending on SKU, but TPM still exists per-instance; recommend a quick Dedicated evaluation if they need sustained high token/sec.

Marta: customer happy for now — they wanted a writeup we can share internally with support playbook and escalation notes. I'll attach this thread to the ticket. thanks all. :raised_hands:
